subject: paper:sonuga-barke-castellanos-2007
quote: spontaneous patterns of very low frequency (<0.1 Hz) coherence within a specific brain network ('default-mode network') thought to support a pattern of generalized task-non-specific cognition during rest, can persist or intrude into periods of active task-specific processing, producing periodic fluctuations in attention that compete with goal-directed activity.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The defining statement of the default-mode interference hypothesis this mechanism node names.

subject: paper:sonuga-barke-castellanos-2007
quote: we explore the putative role of default-mode interference as a cause of performance variability in attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Ties default-mode interference to the reaction-time/performance-variability axis already tracked in the graph — the observable signature of the intrusion model.

subject: paper:castellanos-proal-2012
quote: Recent advances in systems neuroscience-based approaches to brain dysfunction have facilitated the development of models of ADHD pathophysiology that encompass a number of different large-scale resting-state networks.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. States the move from a single prefrontal-striatal locus to distributed large-scale networks — the distributed-not-focal claim.

subject: paper:hoogman-2017-subcortical
quote: The volumes of the accumbens (Cohen's d=-0·15), amygdala (d=-0·19), caudate (d=-0·11), hippocampus (d=-0·11), putamen (d=-0·14), and intracranial volume (d=-0·10) were smaller in individuals with ADHD compared with controls in the mega-analysis.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract; Lancet house style renders the decimal point as a middle dot (·), preserved here. Effect sizes of d ≈ -0.1 to -0.2 are very small — real group differences, not individual markers.

subject: paper:hoogman-2019-cortical
quote: the largest significant effect was for total surface area (Cohen's d=-0.21).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Even the biggest cortical effect is small (d=-0.21), corroborating the subcortical result on a different measure and sample.

subject: paper:hoogman-2019-cortical
quote: Neither surface area nor thickness differences were found in the adolescent or adult groups.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. In adults no cortical differences were detected at all, so structural imaging cannot serve as a diagnostic test in adulthood; medium because it is a group-level null, applied by inference to individual diagnosis.
